request.initial_prompt: Others. Alas for the mother's pain Wasted! Alas the dear Life that was born in vain! Woman, what mak'st thou here, Thou from beyond the Gate Where dim Symplegades Clash in the dark blue seas, The shores where death doth wait? Why hast thou taken on thee, To make us desolate, This anger of misery And guilt of hate? For fierce are the smitings back of blood once shed Where love hath been: God's wrath upon them that kill, And an anguished earth, and the wonder of the dead Haunting as music still. . . .

Others, alas, for the mother's pain wasted. Alas, the dear life that was born in vain.
Woman, what max thou here, thou from beyond the gate where dim simplygades clash in the
dark blue seas, the shores where death doth wait. Why hast thou taken on thee, to make
us desolate, this anger of misery and guilt of hate? For fear saw the smiting's back
of blood once shed where love hath been. Gods wrath upon them that kill, and an anguished
earth, and the wonder of the dead haunting as music still.
